title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 3. Wandering in the Radha Country
html:
Not hearing the name of Hari in the Radha country, the Lord resolves to give up His body; a cowherd boy taught by Nityananda calls out "Hari!"; the Lord sends Chandrashekhara to Navadvipa; Chandrashekhara's account of the Lord's three days of rapture

Verse 1

अथ नत्वा गुरोः पादं तमनुज्ञाप्य माधवः।
तदाज्ञया व्रजन्देशं राढं गूढो महाभुजः॥१॥

atha natvā guroḥ pādaṁ tamanujñāpya mādhavaḥ|
tadājñayā vrajandeśaṁ rāḍhaṁ gūḍho mahābhujaḥ||1||

atha — then; natva — bowing; guroh — of the guru; padam — to the foot; tam — him; anujnapya — taking leave of; madhavah — Madhava; tat-ajnaya — by his command; vrajan — going; desham — to the country; radham — Radha; gudhah — in secret; maha-bhujah — the mighty-armed.

1Then Madhava bowed to His guru's feet, took leave of him and, at his command, set out, keeping Himself hidden, for the Radha country. The mighty-armed one

Verse 2

नित्यावधूतेन सह कृष्णगाथां मुहुर्मुहुः।
पथि गच्छन्लपन्नृत्यन्गायन्स्वभक्तिभावितः॥२॥

nityāvadhūtena saha kṛṣṇagāthāṁ muhurmuhuḥ|
pathi gacchanlapannṛtyangāyansvabhaktibhāvitaḥ||2||

nitya-avadhutena saha — together with Nitya(nanda) the Avadhuta; krishna-gatham — the tale of Krishna; muhuh muhuh — again and again; pathi — on the road; gachchhan — going; lapan — telling; nrityan — dancing; gayan — singing; sva-bhakti-bhavitah — absorbed in His own devotion.

2went along the road together with Nityananda the Avadhuta, telling the tales of Krishna again and again, dancing and singing, absorbed in His own devotion.

Verse 3

ध्यायन्कृष्णपदाम्भोजमात्मनात्मात्मविग्रहम्।
व्रजन्प्रेमाश्रुधाराभिर्निर्झरैर्गिरिशृङ्गवत्॥३॥

dhyāyankṛṣṇapadāmbhojamātmanātmātmavigraham|
vrajanpremāśrudhārābhirnirjharairgiriśṛṅgavat||3||

dhyayan — meditating; krishna-pada-ambhojam — on the lotus feet of Krishna; atmana — within Himself; atma-atma-vigraham — the embodied Self of His self; vrajan — going; prema-ashru-dharabhih — with streams of tears of love; nirjharaih — with waterfalls; giri-shringa-vat — like a mountain peak.

3He walked on, meditating within Himself on the lotus feet of Krishna — the embodied Self of His own self — and with the streams of His tears of love He looked like a mountain peak with waterfalls pouring down it.

Verse 4

विप्लुताक्षः क्वचित्कम्पपुलकाञ्चितविग्रहः।
विह्वलः स्खलितः क्वापि क्वचिद्द्रुतगतिर्व्रजन्॥४॥

viplutākṣaḥ kvacitkampapulakāñcitavigrahaḥ|
vihvalaḥ skhalitaḥ kvāpi kvaciddrutagatirvrajan||4||

vipluta-akshah — His eyes flooded; kvachit — at times; kampa-pulaka-anchita-vigrahah — His body marked with trembling and thrills of rapture; vihvalah — overwhelmed; skhalitah — stumbling; kvapi — at times; kvachit — at times; druta-gatih — with rapid gait; vrajan — going.

4At times His eyes were flooded with tears, at times His body was seized with trembling and thrills of rapture; at times He stumbled in His agitation, and at times He hurried along.

Verse 5

मत्तकरीन्द्रवत्क्वापि तेजसा ववृधे क्वचित्।
क्वचिद्गायति गोविन्द कृष्ण कृष्णेति सादरम्॥५॥

mattakarīndravatkvāpi tejasā vavṛdhe kvacit|
kvacidgāyati govinda kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti sādaram||5||

matta-kari-indra-vat — like a maddened king of elephants; kvapi — at times; tejasa — in might; vavridhe — He grew; kvachit — at times; kvachit — at times; gayati — He sings; govinda — O Govinda; krishna krishna — O Krishna, Krishna; iti — thus; sa-adaram — with reverence.

5At times He moved like a maddened king of elephants, at times He seemed to grow with the might that filled Him, and at times He reverently sang, "Govinda! Krishna! Krishna!"

Verse 6

तत्र देशे हरेर्नामाश्रुत्वा चातीवविह्वलः।
प्रविश्याहं जले क्षिप्रं त्यजामि देहमात्मनः॥६॥

tatra deśe harernāmāśrutvā cātīvavihvalaḥ|
praviśyāhaṁ jale kṣipraṁ tyajāmi dehamātmanaḥ||6||

tatra — in that; deshe — land; hareh — of Hari; nama — the name; ashrutva — not hearing; cha — and; ativa-vihvalah — utterly distraught; pravishya — entering; aham — I; jale — into the water; kshipram — at once; tyajami — shall give up; deham — the body; atmanah — My own.

6Not hearing the name of Hari in that land, He was utterly distraught and said, "I will enter the water at once and give up this body!1

Verse 7

न शृणोमि हरेर्नाम कथं ब्राह्मणसंस्थितिः।
इति निश्चित्य तोयस्य समीपं स व्रजन्प्रभुः॥७॥

na śṛṇomi harernāma kathaṁ brāhmaṇasaṁsthitiḥ|
iti niścitya toyasya samīpaṁ sa vrajanprabhuḥ||7||

na shrinomi — I do not hear; hareh — of Hari; nama — the name; katham — how; brahmana-samsthitih — (is this) a dwelling of brahmanas; iti — thus; nishchitya — resolving; toyasya — to the water; samipam — near; sah — He; vrajan — going; prabhuh — the Lord.

7I do not hear the name of Hari — how can this be a dwelling-place of brahmanas?" Having resolved thus, the Lord went towards the water,

Verse 8

ददर्श बालकांस्तत्र गवां सङ्घविहारिणः।
नित्यानन्दावधूतेन शिक्षितान्हरिकीर्तनम्॥८॥

dadarśa bālakāṁstatra gavāṁ saṅghavihāriṇaḥ|
nityānandāvadhūtena śikṣitānharikīrtanam||8||

dadarsha — He saw; balakan — boys; tatra — there; gavam — with the cows; sangha-viharinah — roaming in a band; nityananda-avadhutena — by Nityananda the Avadhuta; shikshitan — taught; hari-kirtanam — the chanting of Hari.

8and there He saw some boys herding their cows together; Nityananda the Avadhuta had taught them to chant the name of Hari.

Verse 9

तत्रैको बालकोऽत्युच्चं हरिं वद हरिं वद।
इति प्रोवाच हर्षेण पुनः पुनरुदारधीः॥९॥

tatraiko bālako'tyuccaṁ hariṁ vada hariṁ vada|
iti provāca harṣeṇa punaḥ punarudāradhīḥ||9||

tatra — there; ekah — one; balakah — boy; ati-uchcham — very loudly; harim vada — "Say 'Hari'"; harim vada — "Say 'Hari'"; iti — thus; provacha — called out; harshena — joyfully; punah punah — again and again; udara-dhih — noble-minded.

9And one of the boys, a noble-hearted lad, called out joyfully, loudly, again and again: "Say 'Hari'! Say 'Hari'!"

Verse 10

तच्छ्रुत्वा हृषितो देवः संरक्षन्देहमात्मनः।
तत्रैव प्ररुरोदार्तो विह्वलश्चापतद्भुवि॥१०॥

tacchrutvā hṛṣito devaḥ saṁrakṣandehamātmanaḥ|
tatraiva prarurodārto vihvalaścāpatadbhuvi||10||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; hrishitah — delighted; devah — the Lord; samrakshan — preserving; deham — the body; atmanah — His own; tatra eva — right there; praruroda — wept aloud; artah — anguished; vihvalah — overwhelmed; cha — and; apatat — fell; bhuvi — to the ground.

10Hearing this, the Lord was delighted and resolved to preserve His body. But right there He wept aloud in anguish and fell to the ground, overwhelmed.

Verse 11

सान्त्वितश्चावधूतेन वृन्दारण्यस्य वार्तया।
किमद्भुतं ततो गत्वा शिक्षां चक्रे महामतिः॥११॥

sāntvitaścāvadhūtena vṛndāraṇyasya vārtayā|
kimadbhutaṁ tato gatvā śikṣāṁ cakre mahāmatiḥ||11||

santvitah — consoled; cha — and; avadhutena — by the Avadhuta; vrindaranyasya — of Vrindavana; vartaya — with news; kim adbhutam — what a wonder!; tatah — then; gatva — going on; shiksham chakre — gave instruction; maha-matih — the great-minded one.

11The Avadhuta consoled Him with news of Vrindavana. What a wonder! Then, going on, the great-minded Lord gave me2 a charge:

Verse 12

नवद्वीपं प्रगच्छ त्वं मां प्राह श्रीनिकेतनः।
ततोऽहं शोकदुःखार्तो नवद्वीपं व्रजन्नपि॥१२॥

navadvīpaṁ pragaccha tvaṁ māṁ prāha śrīniketanaḥ|
tato'haṁ śokaduḥkhārto navadvīpaṁ vrajannapi||12||

navadvipam — to Navadvipa; pragachchha — go; tvam — you; mam — to me; praha — said; shri-niketanah — the Abode of Shri; tatah — then; aham — I; shoka-duhkha-artah — stricken with grief and sorrow; navadvipam — to Navadvipa; vrajan — going; api — though (already).

12"Go to Navadvipa," the Abode of Shri3 told me. And when I, stricken with grief and sorrow, was already setting out for Navadvipa, He added,

Verse 13

नमो नारायणायेति मद्वाक्यं भक्तसन्निधौ।
वक्तव्यं भवता येन ममानन्दो भविष्यति॥१३॥

namo nārāyaṇāyeti madvākyaṁ bhaktasannidhau|
vaktavyaṁ bhavatā yena mamānando bhaviṣyati||13||

namah narayanaya — "Obeisance to Narayana"; iti — thus; mat-vakyam — My word; bhakta-sannidhau — in the presence of the devotees; vaktavyam — should be spoken; bhavata — by you; yena — whereby; mama — My; anandah — joy; bhavishyati — will be.

13"Give the devotees this word from Me: 'Namo narayanaya'4. That will make Me glad."

Verse 14

श्रुत्वा सर्वं हरेर्वाक्यं गौराङ्गे न्यस्तजीवनः।
स्थितोऽहं परमार्तोऽपि गौरचन्द्रविचेष्टितम्॥१४॥

śrutvā sarvaṁ harervākyaṁ gaurāṅge nyastajīvanaḥ|
sthito'haṁ paramārto'pi gauracandraviceṣṭitam||14||

shrutva — having heard; sarvam — all; hareh — of Hari; vakyam — the word; gaurange — to Gauranga; nyasta-jivanah — having entrusted my life; sthitah — remained; aham — I; parama-artah — in deep distress; api — though; gaurachandra-vicheshtitam — the doings of Gaurachandra.

14I heard all that Hari said, yet I, who had given my life to Gauranga, stayed on, though in deep distress. And Gaurachandra's doings were revealed to me,

Verse 15

ज्ञातं बाह्योपसंक्रान्तं निभृतं परमाद्भुतम्।
सगद्गदं स च प्राह श्रीकृष्णनाममङ्गलम्॥१५॥

jñātaṁ bāhyopasaṁkrāntaṁ nibhṛtaṁ paramādbhutam|
sagadgadaṁ sa ca prāha śrīkṛṣṇanāmamaṅgalam||15||

jnatam — became known (to me); bahya-upasankrantam — what came forth outwardly; nibhritam — what was hidden; parama-adbhutam — most wondrous; sa-gadgadam — in a faltering voice; sah — He; cha — and; praha — uttered; shri-krishna-nama-mangalam — the auspicious name of Sri Krishna.

15both those that came forth outwardly and those that were hidden, all most wondrous. In a faltering voice He kept uttering the auspicious name of Sri Krishna.

Verse 16

हसति स्खलति क्वापि कम्पति गायति क्वचित्।
रोदिति व्रजति क्वापि पतति स्वपिति क्षितौ॥१६॥

hasati skhalati kvāpi kampati gāyati kvacit|
roditi vrajati kvāpi patati svapiti kṣitau||16||

hasati — He laughs; skhalati — stumbles; kvapi — at times; kampati — trembles; gayati — sings; kvachit — at times; roditi — weeps; vrajati — walks; kvapi — at times; patati — falls; svapiti — sleeps; kshitau — on the ground.

16At times He laughs, stumbles, trembles, at times He sings; at times He weeps, wanders off, falls down, or sleeps on the bare ground.

Verse 17

गोपीभावैर्दासभावैरीशभावैः क्वचित्क्वचित्।
आत्मतन्त्रः स्वात्मरतः शिक्षयन्स्वजनानयम्॥१७॥

gopībhāvairdāsabhāvairīśabhāvaiḥ kvacitkvacit|
ātmatantraḥ svātmarataḥ śikṣayansvajanānayam||17||

gopi-bhavaih — in the moods of a gopi; dasa-bhavaih — in the moods of a servant; isha-bhavaih — in the moods of the Lord; kvachit kvachit — now one, now another; atma-tantrah — self-dependent; sva-atma-ratah — delighting in Himself; shikshayan — teaching; sva-janan — His own people; ayam — He.

17Now in the mood of a gopi, now in the mood of a servant, now in the mood of the Lord — so He, self-dependent and delighting in Himself, was teaching His own.

Verse 18

तृतीयदिवसं यावन्न सस्मार स्वविग्रहम्।
महाभीतो व्याकुलोऽहं किं करोमीति चिन्तितः॥१८॥

tṛtīyadivasaṁ yāvanna sasmāra svavigraham|
mahābhīto vyākulo'haṁ kiṁ karomīti cintitaḥ||18||

tritiya-divasam yavat — until the third day; na sasmara — did not remember; sva-vigraham — His own body; maha-bhitah — greatly afraid; vyakulah — anxious; aham — I; kim — what; karomi — shall I do; iti — thus; chintitah — kept thinking.

18Until the third day He did not remember His body, and I, greatly afraid and anxious, kept thinking, "What am I to do?"

Verse 19

ततः परदिने देहं सस्मार मधुसूदनः।
ततोऽहमागतो गेहमाज्ञया न्यासिनां गुरोः॥१९॥

tataḥ paradine dehaṁ sasmāra madhusūdanaḥ|
tato'hamāgato gehamājñayā nyāsināṁ guroḥ||19||

tatah — then; para-dine — on the next day; deham — the body; sasmara — remembered; madhusudanah — Madhusudana; tatah — then; aham — I; agatah — came; geham — home; ajnaya — by the command; nyasinam — of sannyasis; guroh — of the guru.

19Only on the following day did Madhusudana remember His body, and then, at the command of the Guru of sannyasis5, I came home.

Verse 20

आचार्यगेहे श्रीकृष्णः परश्वो वा गमिष्यति।
तत्रैव भवतां भावि दर्शनं तस्य निश्चितम्॥२०॥

ācāryagehe śrīkṛṣṇaḥ paraśvo vā gamiṣyati|
tatraiva bhavatāṁ bhāvi darśanaṁ tasya niścitam||20||

acharya-gehe — to the house of the Acharya; shri-krishnah — Sri Krishna; parashvah — the day after tomorrow; va — perhaps; gamishyati — will come; tatra eva — there indeed; bhavatam — of you; bhavi — will be; darshanam — the sight; tasya — of Him; nishchitam — certainly.

20Sri Krishna will come to the Acharya's house6, perhaps the day after tomorrow; there you will surely see Him.

Verse 21

इति श्रुतं श्रीहरिकीर्तनादिकं
मया च दृष्टं भगवत्कृतं शुभम्।
समग्रमेतत्कथितं सुमङ्गलं
हरेर्गुणं सर्वसुखप्रदं नृणाम्॥२१॥

iti śrutaṁ śrīharikīrtanādikaṁ
mayā ca dṛṣṭaṁ bhagavatkṛtaṁ śubham|
samagrametatkathitaṁ sumaṅgalaṁ
harerguṇaṁ sarvasukhapradaṁ nṛṇām||21||

iti — thus; shrutam — heard; shri-hari-kirtana-adikam — the chanting of Sri Hari and the rest; maya — by me; cha — and; drishtam — seen; bhagavat-kritam — done by Bhagavan; shubham — auspicious; samagram — in full; etat — this; kathitam — has been told; su-mangalam — most auspicious; hareh — of Hari; gunam — the glory; sarva-sukha-pradam — granting every happiness; nrinam — to men.

21Thus have I heard and seen the auspicious chanting of Sri Hari and the other deeds of Bhagavan, and I have told it all in full. This blessed account of Hari's glory grants every happiness to men.

Thus ends the third sarga, "Wandering in the Radha Country" (Radhadesha-bhramana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The Lord speaks in the mood of a devotee for whom life where the name of Hari is not heard is unbearable — an expression of prema, not the despair of a conditioned soul; His body (vv. 10, 18–19) is spiritual, and He, the self-dependent (v. 17), is free to manifest and withdraw it.
  2. From here to the end of the sarga the narrator is Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna, who has returned to the devotees in Navadvipa (cf. Sargas 3.1 and 3.4).
  3. The Abode of Shri (Shriniketana) — an epithet of the Lord as the abode of the goddess Lakshmi.
  4. "Obeisance to Narayana" — the customary greeting of sannyasis: having become a sannyasi, the Lord sends the devotees a greeting according to the rule of His new ashrama.
  5. Apparently the Lord Himself, who has just accepted sannyasa (cf. v. 12).
  6. Advaita Acharya's, at Shantipura.
